sources.note: Exact missing-card status, one border file, one observed interval, and unresolved identity, chronology, and border reviews.

sources.title: Human History Map missing-card queue
sources.note: Confirms that the exact tungus card is independently missing and has no staged draft or assigned packet.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Imported modern ethnolinguistic summary audited and rejected as a direct account of the exact ancient feature.

sources.title: Human History Map 300 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded pre-appearance control for all representative owners and the exact 300 to 200 BCE seam.

sources.title: Human History Map 200 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded exact target geometry, components, islands, owners, direct shared arcs, interval, and feature count.

sources.title: Human History Map 100 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded exact endpoint control showing disappearance and a radically different set of regional labels.

sources.title: Human History Map 1 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded post-end control for later owner changes without an exact Tungus feature.

sources.title: Human History Map Tungus 700 to 1000 card
sources.note: Separate deployed card with different dates, Transbaikal-Amur geometry, Mohe context, and exact association.

sources.title: Human History Map Paleo-Siberian hunter-gatherers card
sources.note: Audited northern neighbor card whose broad identity, chronology, geometry, and evidence cannot replace this target.

sources.title: Human History Map Gojoseon card
sources.note: Audited Korean card with a different exact interval and shape, useful as an association boundary rather than shared copy.

sources.title: Human History Map Xiongnu 200 BCE card
sources.note: Audited western neighbor card with separate imperial history, chronology, geometry, and source contract.

sources.title: Human History Map Proto-Altaic pastoralists card
sources.note: Audited earlier umbrella card warning against equating archaeological material, language families, and broad map polygons.

sources.title: Human History Map Ainu card
sources.note: Audited island neighbor card whose distinct identity and evidence cannot be absorbed into the Tungus polygon.

sources.title: Human History Map researched overrides
sources.note: Confirms the exact id has no override while related tracked cards retain separate association contracts.

sources.title: Poltse archaeological culture
sources.note: Regional heritage authority overview of Poltse sites, settlement forms, food evidence, tools, pottery, burials, and interpretive history.

sources.title: Bayesian phylolinguistics and the internal structure of Transeurasian
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison of widely differing proposed Proto-Tungusic dates and the uncertainty of language-family chronology.

sources.title: History and Culture Hall
sources.note: Jinju National Museum overview distinguishing Korean periods, Samhan communities, Neukdo archaeology, maritime exchange, and varied regional material evidence.

sources.title: On the origin of the ethnonym Tungus
sources.note: Russian Academy study dating the broad spread of Tungus in Russian historical sources to the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

sources.title: The homeland of Proto-Tungusic inferred from contemporary words and ancient genomes
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of homeland proposals, chronology ranges, agriculture vocabulary, ancient genomes, and limits on archaeological identification.

sources.title: Proto-Tungusic in time and space
sources.note: Academic chapter explaining reconstructed vocabulary, time-depth uncertainty, and limits of single-word cultural dating.

sources.title: A radiocarbon chronology of the Poltse I settlement on the Amur River
sources.note: Russian Academy excavation study revising Poltse I dates and distinguishing broad culture chronology from one settlement foundation.

sources.title: Spatial distribution of finds on the eastern outskirts of Poltse I
sources.note: Russian Academy reconstruction of ten dwellings, hearths, vessel placement, ceramics, circulation space, and possible exchange.

sources.title: Scientific analysis of Poltse pottery in Amur and Primorye
sources.note: Peer-reviewed mineralogical, thermal, and diffraction study testing production relationships among Poltse pottery samples.

sources.title: Poltse archaeological culture
sources.note: Russian national encyclopedia reference distinguishing regional stages, settlements, houses, subsistence, crafts, and burial evidence.

sources.title: Cultural change during the late prehistoric period in southern Primorye
sources.note: Russian Academy study separating synchronous Poltse and Krounovka traditions and tracing later interaction through local artifacts.

sources.title: Late Pleistocene-Holocene environmental and cultural changes in Primorye
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional synthesis of Krounovka settlements, agriculture, livestock, hunting, fishing, environmental change, and site density.

sources.title: Evidence of millet agriculture in the Russian Far East
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed direct dating of millet across Primorye and cautious reconstruction of long-term mixed subsistence.

sources.title: Ondol heating at Neukdo and Krounovka sites, 300 to 100 BCE
sources.note: Comparative archaeological study of 49 Korean dwellings, early floor heating forms, dates, clay, and proposed coastal transmission.

sources.title: Archaeological site on Neukdo Island, Sacheon
sources.note: Korean national heritage record for second-century BCE to third-century CE shell mounds, tombs, and dwellings.

sources.title: Craft production at the ancient trade port of Neukdo
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of iron, pottery, maritime work, foreign technology, local consumption, and trade production at Neukdo.

sources.title: Changes in maritime trade and the rise and fall of Neukdo
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology placing Neukdo from the second century BCE onward and its peak port role in the first century BCE.

sources.title: Foreign exchange at the south coast through Neukdo archaeology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study recording Neukdo shell mounds, pottery, metal, bone tools, human remains, and wider maritime connections.

sources.title: Later Joseon and Wiman Joseon chronology
sources.note: National Institute of Korean History page dating Wiman Joseon to 194 BCE and its fall to 108 BCE while distinguishing neighboring polities.

sources.title: Gojoseon and Han war
sources.note: National Institute of Korean History account of the 109 to 108 BCE war, siege, internal division, and fall.

sources.title: Records of the Grand Historian, Account of Chaoxian
sources.note: Digitized Han-period court history for the war against Wiman Joseon, negotiations, internal division, and outsider terminology.

sources.title: Chinese mirror with writing
sources.note: National Museum object page dating an inscribed Chinese-style mirror type to about the first century BCE.

sources.title: Log-coffin burial and Korean-type bronze objects
sources.note: National Museum excavation account of a log coffin, stone-packed pit, pottery, jade, bronze objects, and dating limits.

sources.title: Provenance and distribution networks of the earliest bronze in Primorye
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeometric study of metals, exotic objects, interaction, and the danger of reading style as identity.

sources.title: Functional analysis of Early Iron Age Yankovsky lithics
sources.note: Use-wear study of local stone tools showing how function must be tested rather than guessed from shape.

sources.title: Ethnocultural Atlas of the Amur Region
sources.note: University museum synthesis of Poltse settlement, agriculture, pigs, fishing, hunting, warfare, and contested ethnogenesis.

sources.title: Krounovka 1 excavations in 2002 and 2003
sources.note: Russian Academy bibliographic record for joint excavation and the need to keep separate occupational phases distinct.

sources.title: Burial assemblages of Boisman-2
sources.note: Russian Academy report distinguishing Early Iron Age remains in a dwelling from older family or clan cemeteries at the same site.

sources.title: The archaeological complex of Krounovka-23
sources.note: Scholarly site report used cautiously for local Krounovka archaeology and the limits of incomplete publication.

proposedOverrides.name: Tungus
proposedOverrides.summary: A regional guide that corrects an oversized 200 to 100 BCE Tungus atlas umbrella while preserving distinct Korean, Primorye, and Amur histories.
